text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:

- Vice president of Slovenian government Marjan Podobnik on Wednesday met Jozko Cuk, head of Slovenia's Chamber of Economy, Podobnik said the government would consider demands made by the Chamber of Economy concerning the 1997 budget.
- Parliament a law, according to which Slovenians infected with the HIV virus via blood transfusions, willl be paid compensation.
- Slovenian succession talks delegation said it insisted on an international definition that Yugoslavia broke up in five equal states.
- Railway unions threatened to continue their strike unless demands for higher salaries are met by midnight on Thursday.
- Direct damage caused by railway strike to Slovenia's only port Luka Koper so far is about 300 million tolars ($1.9 million), but the port said it was impossible to estimate the long-term damage.
- Number of overnight stays in Slovenia in April rose to 367,518, an eight percent increase from the previous year, the Slovenian Statistical Office reported.
- The first leg of the soccer cup final between Primorje Ajdovscina and Maribor Branik ended goalless on Wednesday. The second leg will be played in Maribor on June 11.
- Slovenian Constitutional Court is expected to decide on Thursday whether the ratification of Slovenia's association accord with the EU, signed in June last year, is in line with the constitution.
- Parliamentary parties agreed to start a procedure to change Slovenian legislation in line with EU standards, in order to allow foreigners to own real estate in Slovenia.
- Slovenian Defence Minister Tit Turnsek said after his visit to the United States that Slovenia's long-term strategy is to join NATO and that he sees joining as a process and not as an event.
